short: New insights into single-grain mechanical behavior from temp
title: New insights into single-grain mechanical behavior from temperature-dependent 3-D coherent X-ray diffraction

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: How one grain inside a polycrystalline film deforms under thermal load is unmeasured; ensemble diffraction averages over grains. Image one isolated grain by 3-D Bragg coherent X-ray diffraction with a 2x2 um beam and phase retrieval.
states.detail: Absorbed: a1 (HYP/gap), a2 (DES/method), a3 (DES/base_system), a4 (DES/variable_sweep), a5 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The as-deposited selected grain already carries a large inhomogeneous strain at 35 C. Mean out-of-plane strain of the grain rises on heating and falls on cooling along a hysteretic, open loop.
states.detail: Absorbed: a7 (STR/phase/lattice), a8 (STR/phase/lattice), a9 (STR/phase/lattice), a10 (STR/defect/extended). Premises: Bragg-peak centroid shift gives mean lattice strain; peak broadening gives inhomogeneous strain or lattice rotation; Phase jumps or singular lines in a Bragg-CDI phase map mark dislocations or steep displacement gradients

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: The single grain relaxes thermal stress plastically: strain-temperature slope below thermoelastic, loop open. Thermal-mismatch stress in the grain is relaxed by defect activity along x, constrained by its misoriented neighbours
states.detail: Absorbed: a11 (PRP/value), a12 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Film-substrate thermal-expansion mismatch fixes the purely thermoelastic strain-temperature slope

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Temperature-dependent Bragg CDI shows one grain deforming heterogeneously and hysteretically, detail hidden in ensemble averages

nodes.head: xz phase maps: vertical bands, uniform along z; the number of 2pi jumps along x grows on heating

nodes.note: about 1 jump at 50 C, 2-3 at 140 C, ~5 at 240 C (F6c), 3 on cooling at 140 C; edge jumps remain at 50 C after cooling. F6c restored by judge: its 'micrograph' cue is a false scale-bar hit on a phase map (see review.cue_overrides).
